title: Add a built-in debug overlay that displays current performance

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
This can be used to diagnose performance issues, both for developers and players (since this is also available in exported projects). Compared to the editor's **Monitors** tab, this has a few advantages:

- Performance information is overlaid on the running game, so you can still view it while in fullscreen on a single-monitor setup.
- The editor doesn't need to be running in the background, so it works in exported projects where performance is the most indicative of what players will experience.

Press <kbd>F3</kbd> to cycle between 3 modes: hidden, compact (FPS/frametime display only), detailed. This key can be changed in the project settings' input map by modifying `ui_cycle_debug_overlay_display_mode` (remember to enable **Show Built-in Actions**). The debug overlay can also be programmatically shown by changing `SceneTree.debug_overlay_mode` from a script.

The debug overlay's scale automatically adapts to the window size if using the `canvas_items` or `viewport` stretch mode. The default scale is controlled using the `gui/theme/default_theme_scale` project setting.

This PR is a C++ port of the [godot-debug-menu](https://github.com/godot-extended-libraries/godot-debug-menu) add-on I wrote with a few tweaks. Happy holidays :slightly_smiling_face:

- This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/63.

## TODO

- [x] Rename to something else than DebugMenu, e.g. PerformanceOverlay. This "menu" doesn't provide any options you can interact with and it's not really related to *debugging* per se, so a different name would be more suited.
  - Renamed to DebugOverlay.
- [ ] Add a project setting to set the debug overlay mode to use on startup.
- [ ] Add a project setting to change the location the debug overlay appears in? This could be needed for some games where it'd overlap with HUD elements.
  - This could be an enum with 8 positions (top-left, top center, top-right, and so on).
- [ ] Update the graphics settings description whenever any of the graphics settings is changed in RenderingServer. This can likely be done by emitting a signal in RenderingServer and connecting to it in DebugOverlay.
- [ ] Make the graphics settings description more compact somehow? While I've made the C++ port more compact than the add-on by reducing line spacing, it still takes up quite a bit of screen real estate right now.
  - One way to make it more compact is to write abbreviations next to each other, similar to what DuckStation and PCSX2 do with their debug overlays:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5c8c7db-bd74-4aa0-ba83-87734ef761ab)

- [ ] Prevent DebugOverlay nodes from being selectable in the game editor (as they can get in the way). @YeldhamDev Is there some kind of node metadata available for this?

![Debug overlay in game editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/beefc5b7-c851-4f61-9518-71c441584ec0)

- [ ] Figure out the occasional frametime spikes that occur with the detailed view. This is most likely due to graph drawing as commenting it out fixes the issue. Perhaps switching to Image-based drawing like the editor (visual) profiler might work better.
  - This is not a recent engine regression nor an issue specific to the C++ port as the [add-on](https://github.com/godot-extended-libraries/godot-debug-menu) has the same issue, even on 4.2.stable.
